scope: Primary-source mathematical ideas for one-support-image recognition without pretrained weights. These are not direct benchmark comparisons.
novelty_assessment: Gaussian augmentation, covariance distances, invariance regularization and deformable matching are established. Support-derived tolerance combined with constrained part correspondence and counterfactual structural evidence is an experimental combination; originality and superiority are not established.

sources.title: Learning from one and only one shot (Distortable Canvas)
sources.math: Bounded spatial deformation and appearance matching, optimized coarse to fine; deformation cost regularizes similarity.
sources.prior_budget: No extra pretraining; one to ten exemplars per class, evaluated on handwritten characters and sketches including MNIST, EMNIST, Omniglot and QuickDraw.
sources.adoption: Retain a bounded deformation cost when matching support parts.
sources.caveats: Natural-photo abstraction is explicitly future work. Abstract-image results do not establish cluttered-photo category recognition.

sources.title: Mahalanobis++: Improving OOD Detection via Feature Normalization
sources.math: L2 normalization improves Gaussian-distance scoring; class means and shared covariance define Mahalanobis distances.
sources.prior_budget: Evaluates 44 pretrained ImageNet models and estimates statistics from many in-distribution training features.
sources.adoption: Use bounded, strongly shrunk support-augmentation covariance as local nuisance tolerance.
sources.caveats: HyperNet already normalizes descriptors. Synthetic variance is not natural category covariance or a calibrated probability. Blank-part precision must remain bounded.

sources.title: Augmentation Invariant Manifold Learning
sources.status: 2025 revision and JRSSB publication; original preprint 2022
sources.math: A product manifold separates underlying structure from augmentation nuisance; invariant representations estimate the structural coordinate.
sources.prior_budget: Experiments use 60000 MNIST images, 100000 unlabeled STL-10 images and ImageNet pretraining.
sources.adoption: Preserve object structure while learning tolerance to chosen nuisance transformations.
sources.caveats: One reference explores a single augmentation fiber. Additional variants do not reveal differences between members of a category. Guarantees rely on manifold assumptions and multiple underlying samples.

sources.title: LeJEPA: Provable and Scalable Self-Supervised Learning Without the Heuristics
sources.math: SIGReg compares characteristic functions of random feature projections with an isotropic Gaussian target to discourage collapse.
sources.prior_budget: Dataset-scale self-supervised training, including ImageNet; downstream one-shot experiments follow substantial representation training.
sources.adoption: Possible separate unnormalized auxiliary-head ablation; preserve the analytic shape descriptor head.
sources.caveats: A unit-normalized descriptor cannot follow a full Euclidean Gaussian. Distribution regularization does not create missing category observations; this work does not validate strict one-image learning.

sources.title: KerJEPA: Kernel Discrepancies for Euclidean Self-Supervised Learning
sources.math: MMD and kernel Stein discrepancies generalize latent-distribution regularization; analytic alternatives avoid finite-slicing noise. Hyperspherical representations receive separate treatment.
sources.prior_budget: Principal experiment trains ViT-S/8 on ImageNette for 800 epochs, batch 256, four views.
sources.adoption: Prefer small-batch exact regularization over unnecessary random slicing if adding an invariance head.
sources.caveats: Detection and segmentation transfer remain future work. Projector geometry need not describe backbone geometry. No one-image category result.

sources.title: FACTOR: Counterfactual Training-Free Test-Time Adaptation for Open-Vocabulary Object Detection
sources.math: Original-versus-perturbed region predictions quantify attribute sensitivity and drive confidence adjustment.
sources.prior_budget: Frozen pretrained Grounding DINO with Swin visual backbone and BERT text encoder; COCO-C, PASCAL-C and FoggyCityscapes evaluation.
sources.adoption: Compare intact and counterfactual evidence using HyperNet's own features.
sources.caveats: Training-free means no adaptation updates, not no pretraining. Arbitrary part shuffles are not exchangeable statistical nulls. Use a counterfactual margin, not a claimed p-value or causal guarantee.

sources.title: Recurrent connections facilitate occluded object recognition by explaining-away
sources.math: Recognizing an occluder helps explain missing or altered features of the occluded object; benefits depend on computational task organization.
sources.prior_budget: Includes 50000 training composites from 24000 FashionMNIST images and fine-tuned CORnet experiments.
sources.adoption: Use explicit unmatched-part/background explanations in partial matching.
sources.caveats: Neither recurrence alone nor one support image reproduces the reported effect. Sufficiently deep feedforward models can also perform well; no universal recurrent advantage is established.

sources.title: Systematic image perturbations reveal persistent gaps between human and machine vision
sources.status: iScience October 2026 issue; date denotes issue month
sources.math: Controlled perturbations separate global outline, internal parts and texture contributions to recognition.
sources.prior_budget: Tests over 200 networks against humans using 240 exemplars across 48 categories with manually removed backgrounds.
sources.adoption: Diagnose whether scores depend on coherent structure using shuffled-part and texture/shape ablations.
sources.caveats: A diagnostic study, not a one-image recognizer. Its prepared object images do not establish robustness to full-scene background clutter.
